mere-fidelity.title: How to Read Outside Your Tradition
mere-fidelity.description: If you only read what you know you'll agree with, how will you learn? But if you read something from another theological tradition, do you risk weakening your faith? In this episode, James Wood and Joseph Minich explore the importance of reading widely across Christian traditions, the role of ecumenism, and how to deepen your understanding within one's own tradition while remaining open to others. They discuss the value of tradition, truth, and the future of the church in a divided world. — Get 30% of the Baker Book of the Month, The Pursuit of Character: Recovering the Virtues , by going to: http://bakerbookhouse.com/pages/mere-fidelity Register for Beeson Divinity School's 2026 Preaching Conference, July 14-16 in Birmingham, Alabama: https://www.samford.edu/beeson-divinity/preaching-inst

christians-reading-classics.title: The Declaration of Independence with Matthew Spalding and Jake Meador
christians-reading-classics.description: The Declaration of Independence is only a few paragraphs long, but it tries to do something enormous: justify a political break while teaching a moral vision of human equality, liberty, and rightful government. Nadya Williams and Jake Meador sit down with Dr Matthew Spaulding of Hillsdale College, a leading scholar of the Declaration and author of The Making of the American Mind, to read the document as an American classic that still forms our public arguments and our private conscience. — Christians Reading Classics is a podcast from Mere Orthodoxy and is listener-supported.
